liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Not Fade Away** (3 reviews): The jam section of this song is highlighted as particularly powerful; The jam sequence from Not Fade Away through Caution and Feedback is wild [12][15][19]
- **Easy Wind** (1 review): Considered the best performance of this song, featuring great Weir soloing [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-09-20.140664.sbd.boswell.smith.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 28 songs; 173 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd70-09-20.sbd.sacks.1190.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 29 songs; 174 min; rated 3.83/5 by 24 [3]. Said about its sound: Recording levels are excessively high, causing noticeable distortion throughout the audio; Audio is excellent for its age, with only minor vocal and mix changes; Candyman is cut off at the beginning of the track [10][11][13][16][18]
- **gd1970-09-20.sbd.smith.97364.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 29 songs; 177 min; rated 1.67/5 by 3 [4]
- **gd70-09-20.aud.remaster.sirmick.27583.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 27 songs; 167 min; rated 4.72/5 by 97 [6]. Said about its sound: This remaster fixes previous hiss and degradation, though some volume fluctuation remains [21]
- **gd1970-09-20.aud.weinberg.bunjes.81728.flac16**: audience recording; 6 songs; 46 min; rated 2/5 by 3 [8]. Said about its sound: The recording contains a couple of reel stops and volume flaws [8]

## Around the show

- The show concludes with a lullaby performance by the Garcia Gospel Singers [15]
- The acoustic set featured many songs from Workingman's Dead and American Beauty [19]
- David Grisman and David Nelson played mandolin during the first acoustic set [1]
- The NRPS shared the bill with the Grateful Dead [1]
- The acoustic set is considered the best ever, and the electric set is superior [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-09-20.140664.sbd.boswell.smith.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Will Boswell; transferred by Charlie Miller and Matt Smith and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Master Soundboard Reels (borrowed by Peter Kafer) > Will Boswell's reel @ 7 1/2 ips; Transfer Info: Reel (Technics RS1506) > Tascam DA-3000 (DSF… [1]
- **gd70-09-20.sbd.sacks.1190.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Jim Wise and Darrin Sacks; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: The recording is assembled from multiple different source materials [11]
- **gd1970-09-20.sbd.smith.97364.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Matt Smith; source: MR > R Heavily Edited > R @ 71/2ips > CD [4]. Also: Casey Jones and China Cat Sunflower to I Know You Rider come from a specific master; Will's copy was dubbed at 7.5 ips, making it the best possible version [4]
- **gd70-09-20.aud.remaster.sirmick.27583.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jim Wise, Darrin Sacks and SirMick; source: Remastered Soundboard [6]
- **gd1970-09-20.aud.weinberg.bunjes.81728.flac16**: taped by Marty Weinberg; transferred by Jack Warner and Hanno Bunjes; source: recorded by Marty Weinberg on a 5" Uher open-reel deck. [8]. Also: Only the end of the show is available, missing Attics Of My Life [8]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Fillmore East - September 20, 1970](https://www.dead.net/show/september-20-1970) [23]
